name: RIO
description: Intention-oriented object detection aims to detect desired objects based on specific intentions or requirements. For instance, when we desire to "lie down and rest", we instinctively seek out a suitable option such as a "bed" or a "sofa" that can fulfill our needs. Previous work in this area is limited either by the number of intention descriptions or by the affordance vocabulary available for intention objects. These limitations make it challenging to handle intentions in open environments effectively. To facilitate this research, we construct a comprehensive dataset called Reasoning Intention-Oriented Objects (RIO). In particular, RIO is specifically designed to incorporate diverse real-world scenarios and a wide range of object categories. It offers the following key features: 1) intention descriptions in RIO are represented as natural sentences rather than a mere word or verb phrase, making them more practical and meaningful; 2) the intention descriptions are contextually relevant to the scene, enabling a broader range of potential functionalities associated with the objects; 3) the dataset comprises a total of 40,214 images and 130,585 intention-object pairs. With the proposed RIO, we evaluate the ability of some existing models to reason intention-oriented objects in open environments.Submission Number: 57
evaluation_method: mAP (mean Average Precision) / precision-recall for detected intention-objects
reputation: A newly proposed dataset for intention-oriented object detection that is drawing interest for affordance/intention reasoning but is not yet widely adopted.
notes: Large-scale vision benchmark (40k images) with natural-sentence intentions; annotations can be ambiguous (intention subjectivity) and context-dependent; class/intent imbalance possible; non-LLM vision benchmark.
